title: Screen only a valid amount, with the fraud service mocked

blocks.text: A participant that calls an outside service is hard to test against the real thing: it may be slow, down, or unable to give you the verdict you want to check. The page tests such a participant with the service mocked, and tests a validating participant on its own with a fresh `Context`. This participant does both jobs, and the tests you are graded by mock its service exactly that way.

Write `FraudScreeningParticipant`, a jPOS `TransactionParticipant` built from a `FraudService` (declared for you as a nested interface). In `prepare`, read the context entries `amount` and `cardNumber` (strings), then:

items: no amount (or an empty one): put `Amount is missing` in the context entry `error`;
an amount that is not a number: `Invalid amount format`;
an amount that is not positive: `Amount must be positive`.

blocks.text: In each of those cases return `ABORTED` without calling the service: there is no point screening a transaction that is already refused. Otherwise ask the service `isFraudulent(cardNumber, amount)`, with the amount as a `BigDecimal`. A fraud verdict puts `Boolean.TRUE` in `fraudDetected` and returns `ABORTED`; a clean verdict returns `PREPARED` and leaves `fraudDetected` unset.

items: Zero is not a positive amount.
If the service itself fails (it throws), `prepare` must not throw: put `Fraud check unavailable` in `error` and return `ABORTED`.

cases.says: a valid amount is sent to the fraud service with the card number; a clean verdict prepares and a fraud verdict aborts and marks the context
a missing, malformed or negative amount aborts with its own reason, and the fraud service is never called
an amount of zero is rejected as not positive, before any screening
a fraud service that fails aborts the transaction with a reason instead of throwing out of prepare

concepts: A participant that calls an external service is tested with that service mocked, so each verdict, and the calls it should and should not receive, can be set up and checked without a network.
A participant is unit-tested on its own by handing prepare a fresh Context and checking both its answer and what it left in the context, for good input and for each kind of bad input.
